newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's DDI to speed up CDMA cell phone plan.
newsitem.headline: Japan's DDI to speed up CDMA cell phone plan.

text.p: Japanese cellular phone operator DDI Corp said on Tuesday it would switch completely to next-generation digital CDMA cellular phone technology by the end of 1999, moving its schedule forward by two years.
"We need to halt the advance of industry leader NTT Docomo by switching to the new technology faster than we originally planned," a DDI spokesman said.
DDI and Nippon Idou Tsushin Corp, partly owned by Toyota Motor Corp, will joinly begin code division multiple access (CDMA) service in the Osaka area in April 1998.
They had initially planned to launch a nationwide service by 2001.
The stepped-up schedule will not affect DDI's capital investment programme, the spokesman said.

Industry leader NTT Docomo, a cellular phone unit of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp, is gaining momentum in the race to win new subscribers, aided by its nationwide network. It claimed a 53 percent share in May, compared with DDI's 16 percent, dampening DDI's share prices.
